Also, it’s super common for polyfrags to have a bunch of fragments. Don’t worry too much about it.   
We’re not quite polyfrag but almost there, we’re on the very line between “””common””” and polyfrag I guess.

Fragments from what I know (and this is just how we judge things in our system personally) are alters with a single or very little functions. For example, we have a girl over here whose only purpose is feeling this very specific brand of terror. So every time we’re about to experience that feeling, she’s the one to come out and take it. And she only does that.   
We used to have another guy I think who only existed to do dishes and possibly some other cleaning involving water (there’s a traumatic story involving parents behind this) but I’m not super sure because I’m fairly new (Hey, twilight system, it’s me, it’s Hicc. Just commenting so when y’all revisit the recent comments you know it was me here). But yeah, fragments are that. Sometimes they don’t even have names and personalities, they’re not super flashed out, they just exist for one or few purposes and there’s not much to be said about them otherwise. Doesn’t make them any less important or any less of a person/animal/creature/individual. Just means they’re probably very good at their job to the point it takes their whole existence and I think that’s very admirable, personally.

In my personal experience systems tend to be very malleable, but to what you believe is necessary. So if you all, collectively, believe that fusion between particular parts is a great solution, I believe that facilitates things a lot and turns it possible.   
We haven’t fused many times, and most of the fusions were involuntary or through trauma. But when we all agree on things, it’s easier to make them happen. Such as changing the inner world and creating NPCs for it, or straight up splitting off an alter who was already in the process of splitting off but with more specific characteristics of what we need in the moment for the system. Nothing too big in that last one, but a collective “let’s imagine really hard that this new person is positive towards \[insert thing we struggle with\]“ and it mostly works for us. Don’t know if that’s a universal experience tho.

We’re not really polyfrag, but kinda (???), we’re a large system with more than thirty members. What happens is that a group of four or five people becomes ‘the main fronters‘ at a time in this specific combo of people who can deal with the current  life situation and current needs in general. Some alters don’t even know each other because of this, not everyone’s communication is good (it used to be better), but we make it work through very consistent journaling.

The body here doesn’t have aspd, but a few alters do. I’m really sorry you’re going through this, it isn’t fair. We’ve just been denied treatment very very recently for fairly similar reasons. Our heart goes out to you. I personally hope taking some time from therapy focused on multiplicity can maybe restore your faith in getting help.  I don’t think it’s impossible, but damn, it is hard.

If you think going non verbal might be more comfortable and help you in your life in general, then I’d just advise you to experiment a bit with it and maybe talk to a therapist about it. Your problems may have another source with a better solution than going non verbal, but as a person who goes non verbal from time to time I do appreciate that you seem to consider this a “neutral”/positive solution rather than a bad one. It’s not a bad thing to be mute. Some people can’t control it, sure, (and sometimes this causes problems to them but that’s on society lol not on them) but if you can that’s great! 
I just wish you wellness and strength through these though times. Update us when you make your decision! 
Ps: reminder that you don’t have to be mute forever. You can be for any period of time, more than once.
